source.located: Review of Particle Physics (Particle Data Group), u- and d-quark mass summary entries Q002M/Q001M (also Q123UM/Q123DM, mbar Q123MR4, m_u/m_d Q123MR0). The tree's 8.990 = 2(2.16)+4.67 is reproduced EXACTLY by the RPP 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 and 2023 editions and by no other (2018: 9.10; 2024, 2025, 2026: 9.02). Current edition: RPP 2026, F. Takahashi et al., Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 41, 2630011 (2026). The RPP is not on arXiv.

published_statement: PDG 2026 (identical values in 2024 and 2025) summary values: m_u = 2.16 +- 0.07 MeV, m_d = 4.70 +- 0.07 MeV, mbar = (m_u+m_d)/2 = 3.49 +- 0.07 MeV, m_u/m_d = 0.462 +- 0.020. PDG 2019-2023: m_u = 2.16 (+0.49/-0.26 in the RPP; file-rounded +0.5/-0.3), m_d = 4.67 (+0.48/-0.17; file +0.5/-0.2). PDG header text (pdgtext Q123UM, 2026), verbatim: 'The u-, d-, and s-quark masses are estimates of so-called ``current-quark masses,'' in a mass- independent subtraction scheme such as MSbar. The ratios mass(u)/mass(d) and mass(s)/mass(d) are extracted from pion and kaon masses using chiral symmetry. The estimates of d and u masses are not without controversy and remain under active investigation. Within the literature there are even suggestions that the u quark could be essentially massless. ... We have normalized the MSbar masses at a renormalization scale of mu = 2 GeV. Results quoted in the literature at mu = 1 GeV have been rescaled by dividing by 1.35. The values of ``Our Evaluation'' were determined in part via Figures 2 and 3 in the ``Quark masses'' review.' PDG publishes no value for 2m_u + m_d; the sum is the tree's arithmetic on PDG's two entries.
published_hypotheses: current-quark masses in a mass-independent subtraction scheme (MS-bar) -- PDG text
renormalisation scale mu = 2 GeV; literature values at 1 GeV rescaled by 1/1.35 -- PDG text
m_u/m_d and m_s/m_d from pion and kaon masses via chiral symmetry -- PDG text

'Our Evaluation' determined in part from Figures 2 and 3 of the RPP Quark-masses review (an evaluation, not a pure weighted average: the 2026 computed averages are m_u 2.16 +- 0.04, m_d 4.70 +- 0.04, scale factor 1.157 on m_u) -- PDG data rows value_type 'AC'
inputs: lattice QCD (n_f = 2+1 and 2+1+1, some with QED) and sum rules -- PDG footnotes/measurement list
PDG's own caveat: d and u masses 'not without controversy'; 'suggestions that the u quark could be essentially massless'
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED at address.py:77-78 (prose): 'the Higgs supplies 2m_u + m_d = 8.99 MeV of the proton's 938.272 MeV -- 0.96%' drops the MS-bar / mu = 2 GeV qualifier that address.py:426 carries. The numerator is a scheme- and scale-dependent MS-bar mass, the denominator an RG-invariant physical mass; by PDG's own 1.35 rescaling the same sum at mu = 1 GeV is 12.14 MeV = 1.29%, and the F6 factor printed as '24.0' (address.py:80) becomes 18.0 (computed, C8). The tree already disowns the ratio as physics (address.py:83-86: 'a sum of current-quark masses and NOT a Feynman-Hellmann fraction'), so this is a prose-site omission, not a dropped hypothesis of the constant.

ADDED (tree's own, not PDG's) at address.py:77: 'the Higgs supplies' -- attributing the current-quark masses to Yukawa x v is Standard-Model physics the tree adds; PDG says only 'current-quark masses'. Standard, but it is the tree's hypothesis, not the source's.
DROPPED at address.py:426: the EDITION. The comment says 'PDG MS-bar 2 GeV' with no year; the value is RPP 2019-2023 and is superseded by RPP 2024-2026 (m_d 4.67 -> 4.70, sum 8.990 -> 9.02).

DROPPED at address.py:426: the UNCERTAINTY. The tree carries a central value only; RPP 2022 was +1.46/-0.69 MeV on the sum (linear, asymmetric), RPP 2026 is +-0.16 (uncorrelated) / +-0.21 (linear). Computed not to move the conclusion (C7).

DROPPED: PDG's caveat 'the u quark could be essentially massless' (still in the 2026 text). Computed: at m_u = 0 the naive S = 0.50%, the naive factor 45.1, K_mu(H1) = -0.7739, K_mu(H2) = -0.9950 -- still O(1) negative (C9); and one lattice input PDG averages, BAZAVOV 2018 m_u = 2.130 +- 0.041 MeV, excludes m_u = 0 at 52 sigma (C10).

STATUS WORD: address.py:426 marks the value NAMED-NOT-READ; it is now READ at source in PDG's own data release (this audit). The tree's 'valence sum, NOT a Feynman-Hellmann fraction' hypothesis (address.py:85-86) is consistent with PDG's 'current-quark masses' and is not a drift.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0). Parsed PDG's MC tables for RPP 2018-2026 by PDG's stated column layout and PDG's API database for 2024/2025/2026: 8.990 = 2(2.16)+4.67 is reproduced by exactly the RPP 2019-2023 editions (A1); 2024-2026 give 9.02 (A2). PDG's text states MS-bar, mu = 2 GeV, 'current-quark masses', the 1/1.35 rescaling and the m_u = 0 caveat (B1-B5). Re-derived over Fraction the 2/9 exponent (Lambda_3 = Lambda_6^(7/9)(m_c m_b m_t)^(2/27), C0) and reproduced the tree's F6 pin 23.9708 at 8.990 (C1; also read back read-only from address.py: 23.970759811148184); at 9.02 the factor is 23.894 (C2). K_mu unchanged at 4 dp (C6) and O(1) negative across every tested input (C7, C9). One PDG-internal DISCREPANCY recorded, not a refutation: (m_u+m_d)/2 from the summary m_u, m_d is 3.43 MeV against PDG's own mbar 3.49 +- 0.07, and 2 mbar (2r+1)/(1+r) = 9.19 MeV against 9.02 from the individual entries (B8) -- within PDG's quoted errors; PDG's 'Our Evaluation' is not a single fit.

lacked_data: For THIS result M's hypothesis is testable and the evidence is AGAINST it moving anything. The value the tree uses (RPP 2019-2023) was built before BAZAVOV 2018 fully tightened the average and before ALEXANDROU 2021 / BRUNO 2020; later data (RPP 2024+) moved m_d by +0.03 MeV and cut the errors ~5x, i.e. the earlier authors did lack data, and having it moved the sum by +0.33% (0.19 current sigma). Computed: that shifts the naive factor 23.97 -> 23.89 and leaves K_mu = -0.7703 (H1) / -0.9904 (H2) unchanged at 4 dp; even the extreme PDG caveat m_u = 0 leaves K_mu O(1) negative. What the data did NOT supply, and could not: the ratio (2m_u+m_d)/m_p is convention-dependent (0.96% at 2 GeV, 1.29% at 1 GeV by PDG's own factor), so no new measurement makes it a physical 'Higgs share' -- that limit is a hypothesis (the MS-bar scale), not missing data, and the tree already names it at address.py:83-86 and 426.
grade_evidence: Statement READ at source in PDG's own data release: 8.990 = 2(2.16)+4.67 is exactly the RPP 2019-2023 value, MS-bar at mu = 2 GeV, current-quark masses (PDG text, verbatim). The tree's hypotheses (MS-bar 2 GeV; valence sum, not a Feynman-Hellmann fraction) agree with PDG's. Re-derivation agrees (ALL PASS). The datum HAS moved (RPP 2024-2026: 9.02 +- 0.16) but the move is -0.19 sigma and moves no conclusion: '0.96%' prints the same, K_mu is unchanged at 4 dp, and the finding it supports (F6: the naive factor ~24 is S-dependent, 3-4.5 at sigma-term values) survives. RECORDED, NOT REPAIRED: (i) stale edition -- the constant is RPP 2019-2023, current is 9.02; (ii) the tree's 1e-5 selftest pin 23.9708 is edition-specific and would reject the current input (23.894), and address.py:80's printed '24.0' would print '23.9'; (iii) address.py:77-78 prose omits the MS-bar/2 GeV qualifier, and the '24' is a 2-GeV-convention number (18.0 at 1 GeV); (iv) PDG-internal: summary m_u, m_d imply mbar 3.43 against PDG's 3.49 +- 0.07. None is a refutation; none is WRONG.
what_would_change_the_grade: -> DATA-DEPENDENT if the docket counts the 4-significant-figure pinned factor 23.9708 (address.py selftest) as a conclusion, since it moves with the edition (23.894 at RPP 2024+). -> NARROWED if the prose claim at address.py:77-78 ('the Higgs supplies ... 0.96%') is read as a physical statement rather than the labelled naive reading, since it holds only in the MS-bar mu = 2 GeV convention. -> reconsidered if FLAG 2024 or the RPP Quark-masses review, read at source, gave a light-quark sum differing from 9.02 by more than ~50% (the size needed to take S_valence near a sigma-term value) -- no input in PDG's 2026 measurement list comes near that.
